newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends lower, dragged by NYMEX gasoline.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends lower, dragged by NYMEX gasoline.

text.p: September IPE Brent crude oil ended Monday softer after following NYMEX products for most of the afternoon.
The prompt September Brent closed for the day down some 11 cents at $18.42 a barrel, just a few cents up from the intra-day low of $18.35.

"Who knows where it (Brent) is going? It's been up and down like a yo-yo for the day, dragged by (NYMEX) gasoline. A dip in the (NYMEX) gasoline took the strength out at the end (of trade)," one broker said.

August unleaded gasoline on the NYMEX ended the day up over half a cent at 64.60 cents a gallon, but still down more than half a cent for its days high. U.S. traders attributed the gains in part to a pre-expiry squeeze.
The contract is due to expire on Thursday.
NYMEX heating oil also gained ground over the day.
"The U.S. products still look good but I don't expect to see much movement from here. We're comfortable at these figures," another broker commented.

Rumours of a possible problem at the Venezuelan Punta Cardon refinery helped boost NYMEX gasoline to its high earlier, a U.S. based trader said. The contract slipped back on news that only a small problem had been detected at the refinery.
Earlier news that Iraq was about to submit annexes to the United Nations on its aid distribution plan triggered a selloff.

Nizar Hamdoon, Iraq's ambassador to the U.N. said on Monday that Iraq had delivered the annexes to the U.N. He also said Iraq still hoped the U.N. would change its mind and allow Baghdad to make up time lost since June 8 by putting back the start date for the oil sales.

A senior U.N. official said on Monday that the U.N. Security Council late last week ruled out moving forward the start date for the Iraqi oil sales under the second round of their "oil-for-food" deal.
Prompt August gas oil ended Monday's trading earlier down some 50 cents at $167 a tonne having tracked Brent for the day.
